newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa says doctors should let her go home.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa says doctors should let her go home.

text.p: A jestful Mother Teresa poked fun at herself on Monday, saying she was making life difficult for her doctors and it was time they let her go home.
Doctors said the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun's health was improving following heart surgery, and some brief pain she experienced overnight was not related to her cardiac trouble.

"Mother Teresa's cardiac status continues to stabilise under close monitoring," a team of doctors treating the revered missionary at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in a regular medical bulletin.
They said Mother Teresa, who had been in critical condition following heart surgery on November 29, was alert and cooperative, and that her sense of humour was in evidence.

"Doctors, I think now I am more difficult than critical -- I better go home. I will take Dr Patricia with me," it quoted the 1979 Nobel peace prize winner as saying in a reference to Patricia Aubanel, an American doctor on the medical team.
"She's better today. She's blessing everyone," said a member of Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity religious order who visited the nun briefly. "She blessed me. She's very happy."
An earlier bulletin said Mother Teresa had experienced brief discomfort overnight but then went back to sleep.
"She was uncomfortable at 0100 hrs (1930 GMT Sunday) for two or three minutes," the bulletin said. "After that she was all right. Otherwise, Mother (Teresa) had a good sleep."
"There was one (pain), but it had nothing to do with her cardiac status," clinic official A.K. Chatterjee told reporters, saying it could have been gastric pain.
Earlier, Dr Tarun Praharaj, a member of the medical team, said the pain could have been due to her bronchial pneumonia.
Doctors on Sunday said Mother Teresa had suffered a slight setback and her bronchial pneumonia was not responding to treatment.
During the previous week, long-standing lung and kidney problems combined with an irregular heartbeat to complicate her recovery from her third heart surgery in five years.
Over the weekend, doctors decided to postpone a procedure aimed at stabilising Mother Teresa's heartbeat. They wanted to wait until she gained strength.
The doctors have warned that Mother Teresa's recovery might take a long time, and that she may never be as active as before.

Thousands of people all over the world revere Mother Teresa as a saint for her work with the ill, the poor and the dying. The Missionaries of Charity religious order she founded runs 456 charitable homes in 111 countries.
